crossRefs.note: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?
though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.
“My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, and the grave is ready for me.
if I have said to corruption, ‘You are my father;’ to the worm, ‘My mother,’ and ‘My sister,’
Behold, you have made my days hand widths. My lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely every man stands as a breath.”
You sweep them away as they sleep. In the morning they sprout like new grass.
He weakened my strength along the course. He shortened my days.
For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.

translations.web: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
translations.bsb: What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my future, that I should be patient?
translations.kjv: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?
translations.asv: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is mine end, that I should be patient?
